license_rule: Vendored third-party code must be MIT or Apache-2.0. Checked 2026-10-13 against each project's own repo/package, not a summary's claim.

methods.name: scroll-animation
methods.description: Scroll reveals, staggers, parallax and counters from house atoms: reveal.js (entrances), motion.js (stagger, parallax, count-up). Content is visible by default; reduced motion renders static.

inputs.target_elements: CSS selector or markup marked .reveal / data-parallax / data-count-to
inputs.animation_type: up | down | left | right | zoom | fade | stagger | parallax | count-up

methods.outputs: markup attributes plus assets/reveal.{js,css} and assets/motion.js, vendored into the site's /assets
methods.source_reference: https://gsap.com/docs/v3/ (studied for scope only; no GSAP code used)

license.note: GSAP npm 3.15.0 declares "Standard 'no charge' license: https://gsap.com/standard-license", which is not MIT/Apache-2.0, so GSAP is not vendored. Using GSAP itself needs an owner decision.

methods.name: lenis-smooth-scroll
methods.description: Optional smooth scrolling for marketing/content sites longer than one viewport. Default off for app/admin/dashboard/tool/portal; off under prefers-reduced-motion; native scroll whenever Lenis is not vendored.
methods.outputs: an initialized Lenis instance driven by requestAnimationFrame (assets/smooth-scroll.js), or null with a recorded reason

license.note: GitHub license API: MIT (repo pushed 2026-10-02). Vendor the exact pinned dist file; the wrapper never fetches it.

methods.status: shipped-wrapper; lenis dist not yet vendored (a pinned download needs approval per site)

methods.name: react-bits-components
methods.description: Animated hero/text/background/button components adapted to design tokens.

license.note: LICENSE.md is "MIT + Commons Clause License Condition v1.0" (checked 2026-10-13): not MIT-only, so it fails the MIT/Apache-2.0 rule. Owner decision needed to use it. Until then, compose the same effects from house atoms (web-effects-catalog) adapted to the design tokens.

methods.name: website-motion-orchestrator
methods.description: The website build's motion step: after the frontend-design direction is chosen (website-build-standard), select only the motion that fits the site type and content; never impose motion at the expense of usability.
triggers: which animations should this site use
methods.outputs: { methods, atoms, reasons } from assets/motion-select.mjs, then the complete build via website-build-standard
methods.cost: heavy only on selection (the build itself)
